promptTemplate:
Build the following as a new page of this app, reachable at the URL path `/<brief id>`. Keep the pages that already exist working.

## <brief title>

<brief body>

## Constraints

- Work only inside this project directory.
- Use only the dependencies that are already installed; do not add packages.
- Use realistic mock data where the page needs data; there is no backend.
- When you are done, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` must both pass.

brief.title: Invoices
brief.body:
The invoices page of a small-business billing app.

- A table of about 25 invoices: number, customer, issue date, due date, amount and status (draft,
  sent, paid, overdue).
- Filters above the table: a search box that matches invoice number or customer, a status filter
  and a date range for the issue date. Show how many invoices match.
- Amounts are in US dollars and line up so they are easy to compare.
- Each row has a menu with "View", "Download PDF" and "Mark as paid" (only for unpaid invoices).
- When no invoice matches the filters, say so and offer to clear the filters.
- The page must also work on a phone.
brief.markdown:
# Invoices

The invoices page of a small-business billing app.

- A table of about 25 invoices: number, customer, issue date, due date, amount and status (draft,
  sent, paid, overdue).
- Filters above the table: a search box that matches invoice number or customer, a status filter
  and a date range for the issue date. Show how many invoices match.
- Amounts are in US dollars and line up so they are easy to compare.
- Each row has a menu with "View", "Download PDF" and "Mark as paid" (only for unpaid invoices).
- When no invoice matches the filters, say so and offer to clear the filters.
- The page must also work on a phone.

ds.agentResult:
The invoices page is live at `/invoice-list`, and I added an "Invoices" link to the site's top navigation. `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` both pass; the build prints a warning that some bundle files are over 500 kB, which comes from what the app already loads. I haven't opened the page in a browser, so the layout and the PDF download haven't been checked by eye.

**What's on the page**
- **Table:** 25 mock invoices with number, customer, issue date, due date, status and amount in US dollars. The data looks like late September 2026: overdue invoices have due dates in the past and sent ones are due later. Amounts are right-aligned with fixed-width digits so they line up.
- **Filters:** a search box (matches invoice number or customer), a status filter, and "Issued from" / "Issued to" date fields. A count above the table says how many invoices match (e.g. "7 of 25 invoices match"), and screen readers announce it when it changes. A "Clear filters" button appears once any filter is set.
- **Row menu:**
  - **View** opens a popup window with the invoice details.
  - **Download PDF** creates a simple one-page PDF in the browser, since there is no backend.
  - **Mark as paid** only shows for unpaid invoices and changes the status straight away. The change only lasts until the page is reloaded.
- **No matches:** a message says no invoice matches the filters, with a "Clear filters" button.
- **Phone:** filters stack, and the table turns into a list of cards, each with its details and its menu.

**Decisions for you**
- **Drafts can be marked as paid.** I read "unpaid" as anything not yet paid, so drafts get the option too. If only sent and overdue invoices should have it, that's a one-line change.
- **Plain date fields for the date range.** I used the browser's own date inputs rather than the design system's calendar, because they are simpler and work well on phones. I can switch to the calendar if you want the in-page picker.

The table, empty state and page header follow

brief.title: Notification settings
brief.body:
A settings page where a signed-in user of a team chat app decides which notifications they get.

- Three groups: "Messages" (direct messages, mentions, replies in threads you follow), "Channels"
  (new channels, channel invites) and "Account" (security alerts, product news).
- Each notification has a short description and a switch per delivery channel: email, push and
  in-app.
- Security alerts by email cannot be turned off; say why.
- A "Quiet hours" section with a switch and a start and end time.
- Changes are not saved until the user presses "Save changes". The button is disabled until
  something changes and shows progress while saving (fake it with a one-second delay), and a short
  confirmation appears when the save succeeds. A "Discard" action resets the form.

# Notification settings

A settings page where a signed-in user of a team chat app decides which notifications they get.

- Three groups: "Messages" (direct messages, mentions, replies in threads you follow), "Channels"
  (new channels, channel invites) and "Account" (security alerts, product news).
- Each notification has a short description and a switch per delivery channel: email, push and
  in-app.
- Security alerts by email cannot be turned off; say why.
- A "Quiet hours" section with a switch and a start and end time.
- Changes are not saved until the user presses "Save changes". The button is disabled until
  something changes and shows progress while saving (fake it with a one-second delay), and a short
  confirmation appears when the save succeeds. A "Discard" action resets the form.

brief.title: First project
brief.body:
What a new user of a design feedback tool sees right after signing up, before they have any
projects.

- The page explains in one or two sentences what a project is and why they would create one.
- One primary action, "Create your first project", and a secondary way to "Import from Figma".
- Below it, a short checklist of three getting-started steps (create a project, invite a teammate,
  share a link for feedback), each with a one-line explanation. The first step is the current one;
  the others are not done yet.
- A link to a two-minute video tour.
- Pressing "Create your first project" opens a small dialog that asks for a project name and
  creates it. After that, the page shows the new project in a list and the checklist marks the
  first step done.

brief.title: Sign in
brief.body:
A sign-in page for a project management tool called Tally.

- A centered card with the product name, a short welcome line, an email field, a password field
  and a "Sign in" button.
- A "Forgot password?" link next to the password field and a "Create an account" link below the
  card.
- A "Keep me signed in" checkbox.
- Submitting with an empty or malformed email shows an error on that field. Any password other
  than `correct-horse` shows "Email or password is incorrect" above the button.
- While the request is in flight (fake it with a one-second delay), the button shows that it is
  working and cannot be pressed twice.
brief.markdown:
# Sign in

A sign-in page for a project management tool called Tally.

- A centered card with the product name, a short welcome line, an email field, a password field
  and a "Sign in" button.
- A "Forgot password?" link next to the password field and a "Create an account" link below the
  card.
- A "Keep me signed in" checkbox.
- Submitting with an empty or malformed email shows an error on that field. Any password other
  than `correct-horse` shows "Email or password is incorrect" above the button.
- While the request is in flight (fake it with a one-second delay), the button shows that it is
  working and cannot be pressed twice.

The Tally sign-in page is now at `/sign-in`, and the existing pages and routes haven't changed. `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` both pass; the build prints a warning that one bundle is larger than 500 kB, but it doesn't fail. I haven't opened the page in a browser, so the form behaviour is untested.

I built it from the design system's sign-in page and auth card templates, with these changes to match your spec:

- **Card:** centred, with "Tally" as the page heading and a short welcome line. It sits inside the site's normal header and footer.
- **Email errors:** submitting an empty email shows "Enter your email address." on the field. A malformed one shows "Enter an email address like name@example.com." Either way the cursor moves to the email field.
- **Password:** any password other than `correct-horse` shows "Email or password is incorrect" above the button. I moved that message there from the top of the form, where the template had it.
- **While it's working:** the fake request takes one second. The button shows it's loading, and extra clicks during that second are ignored.

- **Success:** your spec didn't say what happens after a correct password, so I added a "You are signed in" message that replaces the form.

I built the Tally sign-in page at `/sign-in`, and `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` both pass. I haven't opened it in a browser, so I haven't seen the layout or tried the error messages and loading state myself.

**What changed**
- `src/SignIn.tsx` is the new page.
- `src/main.tsx` now shows the sign-in page when the URL is `/sign-in` (a trailing slash also works) and the existing home page for every other URL. No router package is installed, so I added this small check instead of adding one. `/sign-in` will load under `pnpm dev` and `pnpm preview`. A real deployment would need its server set to send all URLs to `index.html`.

**How it behaves**
- **Email check:** an empty or malformed email shows a red error under the email field and puts the cursor back there. The error clears as soon as you type.
- **Password check:** any password other than `correct-horse` shows "Email or password is incorrect" above the button. It also clears the password field.
- **While signing in:** there's a one-second fake delay. The button is disabled and shows a spinner with "Signing in…", so it can't be pressed twice.
- **On success:** the card changes to a "You're signed in" message with the email, and a "Go to your projects" link to `/`.

**Things I added beyond the spec**
- A "Show password" eye button in the password field.
- "Keep me signed in" is ticked by default. It only changes the wording of the success message, since there's no backend to remember a session.

**Links with no page behind them yet:** "Forgot password?" goes to `/forgot-password` and "Create an account" goes to `/sign-up`. Neither page exists, so for now both just show the existing home page.

scores.evidence: All gaps come from the Tailwind scale, but the card mixes too many steps: mt-1, mt-1.5, space-y-5, mt-6 and mb-6. The steps still grow with grouping (label to input 1.5, between fields 5, between sections 6).

The 'Welcome back' h1 is text-xl font-semibold over a text-sm muted subtitle, and the full-width indigo 'Sign in' button is the only filled action. 'Forgot password?' and 'Create an account' step down to text links.

The heading, labels, inputs, checkbox row and button all start on the card's p-8 left edge. The 'Password' label and 'Forgot password?' link share one row through flex justify-between, and the eye toggle sits inside the input's right padding.

Empty and malformed email each get their own message under the field, with a CircleAlert icon and aria-invalid. A wrong password shows a role=alert box above the button. During the request the button is disabled and shows a spinner with 'Signing in…', and success shows a 'You're signed in' view with a next step.
The only animation is animate-spin on the LoaderCircle, and it shows progress while the request is in flight. Nothing animates on page load.

Every input has a label linked with htmlFor, the email error is tied to its field with aria-describedby, and the form error uses role=alert with an icon. The password toggle is a real button with aria-label and aria-pressed, focus rings are visible, and focus moves to the field that failed.

Colors are Tailwind palette classes rather than role tokens: bg-slate-50, text-slate-600, bg-indigo-600, border-red-500, bg-red-50 and text-emerald-600. Controls are raw elements styled by hand instead of themed components.

The steps are few and grow with grouping: gap-1 between title and description, FieldGroup's default gap between fields, gap-6 between the card's sections, and gap-6 between the card and the 'Create an account' line.

CardTitle is rendered as an h1 'Tally' at text-2xl in font-heading, above a muted CardDescription. The only primary action is Button variant="primary"; both links are plain underlined text in foreground color.

The title, labels, inputs and full-width button share the CardContent left edge. The 'Password' label and 'Forgot password?' link share a baseline through flex items-baseline, and the checkbox row uses Field orientation="horizontal".

Empty and malformed email each get a FieldError under the field, with data-invalid and aria-invalid set. A wrong password shows an error Alert above the button saying how to recover ('Check them and try again, or reset your password'). The button uses loading={pending}, and success shows a success Alert.
No custom animation is added. Motion comes only from component defaults, such as the Button loading state, so it uses the system tokens.

FieldLabel is linked to every Input and to the Checkbox, the page has one h1, and FieldError is tied to the email field with aria-describedby. Both alerts pair an icon with text, links are underlined rather than marked by color alone, and focus returns to the email field when validation fails.

Everything is built from @atom63/ui-react components: Card, Field, Input, Checkbox, Alert and Button. The only className additions use tokens (text-muted-foreground, text-foreground, gap-6, text-2xl), and there are no literal colors or one-off lengths.
